facts.raw_span: Initial serum troponin I level: 0.070 ng/mL
Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
Negative P waves in lead I
Initial serum troponin I level: 0.070 ng/mL

Negative P waves in lead I

concepts.why: The patient presented with chest pain, elevated serum troponin I level, and total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, which are all indicative of an acute myocardial infarction.
The patient's right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, and left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side, which is consistent with dextrocardia.
The patient has a total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, which is a common finding in coronary artery disease.
The patient's organs are reversed, with the right atrium and right ventricle on the left side, and left atrium and left ventricle on the right side, which is consistent with sitrus inversus.

rationales.F01: Chest pain is a common symptom of acute myocardial infarction.
rationales.F08: Elevated troponin levels are a strong indicator of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F09: Total occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery is a strong indicator of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction.
rationales.F10: The presence of situs inversus and dextrocardia is indicated by the abnormal positioning of the heart chambers.
rationales.F11: ST-segment elevations are a common sign of myocardial infarction.
rationales.F12: Negative P waves in lead I can indicate dextrocardia or other cardiac anomalies.
